items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls; the program resends the history each time. Options b and c treat the model as having its own memory, and d treats the window as permanent.

Call 1 sends 2,000 + 100 = 2,100. Call 2 sends those plus the 50-token request and 400-token result: 2,550. Total 4,650. An answer of 2,550 counts only the last call; 2,500 or 4,600 forgets part of the history.

Memory across sessions needs storage outside the model, read back into the window by the program or a tool. A larger window or an old chat does not persist, and shared instructions cannot hold each student's data.

items.answer: It costs tokens on every call and a bloated context makes the model recall worse; retrieve only the relevant page instead.
